content: 1. Ethinyl Estradiol and Atazanavir: Atazanavir can either increase or decrease the levels of norethindrone by affecting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 2. Atazanavir and Norgestimate: Atazanavir may alter the levels of norgestimate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments or close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be used if possible. 3. Cobicistat and Norgestrel: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 4. Atazanavir and Nortiptyline: Atazanavir increases the levels of nortriptyline through an unspecified mechanism. Cobicistat also increases nortriptyline levels. Careful dose titration of the antidepressant is recommended, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring its response during coadministration. 5. Cobicistat and Oliceridine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. 6. Atazanavir and Oliceridine: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions as with cobicistat apply. 7. Cobicistat and Omeprazole: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Atazanavir and Ondansetron: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. 9. Cobicistat and Ondansetron: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Orlistat and Atazanavir: Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely, as loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if an increased viral load is confirmed. 11. Cobicistat and Osilodrostat: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Monitor closely. 12. Atazanavir and Osilodrostat: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar dose reduction and monitoring recommendations apply. 13. Atazanavir and Ospemifene: Atazanavir increases the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cobicistat and Oxycodone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the dose as needed. 15. Atazanavir and Panobinostat: Atazanavir increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 16. Cobicistat and Paclitaxel: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Cobicistat and Paricalcitol: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is potential for increased toxicity. 18. Atazanavir and Paricalcitol: Atazanavir increases the levels of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 19. Cobicistat and Paroxetine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paroxetine through an unspecified mechanism. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring its response during coadministration. 20. Atazanavir and Penbutolol: Atazanavir increases the effects of penbutolol through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is an increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 21. Atazanavir and Perampanel: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat and Perphenazine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of perphenazine through an unspecified mechanism. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be needed upon coadministration. Monitor closely. 23. Atazanavir and Pindolol: Atazanavir increases the effects of pindolol through pharmacodynamic synergism. Similar precautions as with penbutolol apply. 24. Cobicistat and Pitavastatin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Start with the lowest recommended dose of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors that are not contraindicated with cobicistat, and titrate while monitoring for safety. 25. Cobicistat and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is a CYP3A4 substrate. Monitor closely for increased toxicities. 26. Atazanavir and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 27. Atazanavir and Pramlintide: Atazanavir decreases the effects of pramlintide through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 28. Cobicistat and Pravastatin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pravastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Start with the lowest recommended dose of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors that are not contraindicated with cobicistat, and titrate while monitoring for safety. 29. Cobicistat and Praziquantel: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Atazanavir and Praziquantel: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 31. Atazanavir and Prednisolone: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cobicistat and Propafenone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended upon coadministration with antiarrhythmics. 33. Atazanavir and Prednisone: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Atazanavir and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel): Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Atazanavir and Progesterone (Micronized): Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Atazanavir and Progesterone (Natural): Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Atazanavir and Protriptyline: Atazanavir increases the levels of protriptyline through an unspecified mechanism. Cobicistat also increases protriptyline levels. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring its response during coadministration. 38. Cobicistat and Quazepam: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Atazanavir and Quinidine: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cobicistat and Quinidine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinidine through an unspecified mechanism. Quinidine is a substrate of CYP3A4 and P-gp, and cobicistat is a substrate and inhibitor of both enzymes. Monitor closely. 41. Cobicistat and Quinine: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Cobicistat and Quizartinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose of quizartinib when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Monitor closely. 43. Atazanavir and Quizartinib: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar dose reduction and monitoring recommendations apply. 44. Cobicistat and Rabeprazole: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Atazanavir and Repaglinide: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cobicistat and Repaglinide: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ribociclib and Atazanavir: Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Atazanavir and Rifabutin: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the rifabutin dose by up to 75% (e.g., 150 mg every other day or three times per week). Monitor for rifabutin-associated neutropenia and uveitis. 49. Rifabutin and Atazanavir: Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 50. Rifabutin and Cobicistat: Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg every other day when coadministered with cobicistat. Monitor closely. 51. Cobicistat and Rifabutin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rifabutin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg every other day. Monitor for rifabutin-associated neutropenia and uveitis. 52. Atazanavir and Rilpivirine: Atazanavir increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Cobicistat and Ripretinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 54. Atazanavir and Ripretinib: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 55. Cobicistat and Risperidone: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of risperidone through an unspecified mechanism. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be needed upon coadministration. Monitor closely. 56. Atazanavir and Ritonavir: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Atazanavir and Rivaroxaban: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Cobicistat and Roflumilast: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Cobicistat and Roflumilast (Topical): Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of topical roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Atazanavir and Roflumilast (Topical): Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of topical roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Cobicistat and Romidepsin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Atazanavir and Ropivacaine: Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Atazanavir and Rosiglitazone: Atazanavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 64. Atazanavir and Rosuvastatin: Atazanavir increases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is potential for increased toxicity. Alternatives should be considered if available. 65. Cobicistat and Rosuvastatin: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. Monitor closely. 66. Rucaparib and Cobicistat: Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 67. Rucaparib and Atazanavir: Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 68. Atazanavir and Salmeterol: Atazanavir increases the levels of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as there is potential for increased toxicity. Alternatives should be considered if available. 69. Cobicistat and Seladelpar: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 70. Atazanavir and Seladelpar: Atazanavir increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Cobicistat and Selexipag: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of selexipag through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor closely for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 72. Cobicistat and Selpercatinib: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose of selpercatinib if coadministration is necessary. Monitor closely for side effects. 73. Atazanavir and Sertraline: Atazanavir increases the levels of sertraline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Cobicistat and Sertraline: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sertraline through an unspecified mechanism. Carefully titrate the dose of the antidepressant to the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring its response during coadministration. 75. Cobicistat and Sirolimus: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 76. Atazanavir and Sitagliptin: Atazanavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 77. Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate and Atazanavir: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Monitor closely. 78. Atazanavir and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Atazanavir increases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Atazanavir and Solifenacin: Atazanavir increases the levels of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Atazanavir and Sonidegib: Atazanavir increases the levels of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If necessary, administer the inhibitor for less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal effects. 81. Atazanavir and Sorafenib: Atazanavir increases the levels of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Stiripentol and Atazanavir: Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 83. Stiripentol and Cobicistat: Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 84. Cobicistat and Sufentanil: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 85. Atazanavir and Sufentanil SL: Atazanavir increases the levels of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 86. Cobicistat and Sufentanil SL: Cobicistat increases the levels of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 87. Atazanavir and Sunitinib: Atazanavir increases the levels of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 88. Atazanavir and Tacrolimus: Atazanavir increases the levels of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 89. Cobicistat and Tacrolimus: Cobicistat increases the levels of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 90. Atazanavir and Tadalafil: Atazanavir increases the levels of tadalafil by decreasing its metabolism. Stop tadalafil more than 24 hours before protease inhibitor initiation, restart 7 days after initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 91. Tazemetostat and Cobicistat: Tazemetostat decreases the levels of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 92. Atazanavir and Tasimelteon: Atazanavir increases the levels of tasimelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 93. Tazemetostat and Atazanavir: Tazemetostat decreases the levels of atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 94. Tecovirimat and Atazanavir: Tecovirimat decreases the levels of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 95. Tecovirimat and Cobicistat: Tecovirimat decreases the levels of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 96. Atazanavir and Temsirolimus: Atazanavir increases the levels of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 97. Cobicistat and Temsirolimus: Cobicistat increases the levels of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions apply. 98. Atazanavir and Teniposide: Atazanavir increases the levels of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 99. Cobicistat and Terbinafine: Cobicistat increases the levels of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 100. Atazanavir and Tenofovir DF: Atazanavir and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism, potentially resulting in loss of antiviral activity. Ritonavir boosting may help compensate. 101. Atazanavir and Terbinafine: Atazanavir increases the levels of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
